## 8a6282b87245

**Reproduced defect: collision-aware packing is absent from generated support.** Audited generator SHA: `8576b8c1227a2e895a5629239d28ef4685715a9d3fc7ae5be012d0df4511bfdb`; selected rule hash: `af694b46412a`.

The intended rule classifies exact rectangular frames versus nonframes, moves frames upward and nonframes downward, and packs each class at the first collision-free row. The generator's `used_cols` policy instead makes every object's column extent disjoint from every other object's extent, so the collision-search branch can never matter.

I sampled 60 generated inputs, 20 per band. Zero of 60 contained any pair of overlapping object column spans. A shortcut that independently snaps every frame to row 0 and every nonframe to the bottom—with no collision search or dense packing—matched the selected Racket output on all 60/60 inputs.

The separating input is a valid 14×15 grid with two 3×3 frames in the same columns 4–6, one at rows 2–4 and one at rows 8–10. `self_check` returns no errors. The selected rule stacks color 2 at rows 0–2 and color 3 at rows 3–5; the independent-edge rival places both at rows 0–2 and overwrites the first, differing in 16 cells.

Exact input, outputs, per-sample measurements, and commands: `checks/audit/8a6282b87245/reproduction.json`. Supporting files: `checks/audit/8a6282b87245/input.json`, `racket.json`, `rival.json`, `generated_inputs.json`, `generated_racket.json`, and reusable probe `analyze_shortcut.py`. The combined audit check also found no task-local tests and no semantic contract: `checks/audit/8a6282b87245-combined/checks/8a6282b87245_audit_summary.json`.

No source files for this audit target were changed.
